commit_policy: NO dataset pixels are committed to the repo; fetch.sh re-downloads and verifies SHA-256.

datasets.name: Mark Fairchild's HDR Photographic Survey (HDRPS)
datasets.licence: Copyright 2006-2007 Mark D. Fairchild, all rights reserved; 'made publicly available, free of charge, for research purposes and non-commercial publication in research journals, presentations, and conference proceedings. Any commercial publication of these images is prohibited.' Acknowledge "Mark Fairchild's HDR Photographic Survey". (http://markfairchild.org/HDR.html)
datasets.redistribution: NO (all rights reserved; research use only) -> fetch script only
datasets.absolute_luminance: YES per scene: 'Luminance multipliers to convert the OpenEXR data to absolute luminance are included in the data files or on the web page itself'; 28 scenes also have Minolta CS-100 spot measurements (Y,x,y) and appearance scaling
datasets.camera: Nikon D2x (4288x2848, 23.7x15.7 mm DX CMOS), mostly Nikkor 17-55 mm f/2.8; NEF->16-bit TIFF (Photoshop CS2 raw) -> Photoshop 'merge to HDR', white-balanced to in-camera white point (CIC15HDRSurvey.pdf)
datasets.bit_depth: OpenEXR half (16-bit float), PIZ, RGB (checked with oiiotool --info)
datasets.known_defect: hard ceiling from the HDR merge: every scene checked has a plateau at the raw max (GoldenGate(2) 128.875, Zentrum 171.875, McKeesPub 45.78, OCanadaLights 93.94); lamp cores are clipped -> source luminance/energy are lower bounds. WaffleHouse has 19 % zero pixels (crushed shadows). Negative channel values exist (matrix/merge).

datasets.name: MPI HDR video (Tunnel, Highway; Krawczyk)
datasets.claims_unverified: search-result summary of that page: Tunnel = drive through a small tunnel in Saarbruecken, Highway = highway near Saarbruecken facing the sun, captured by G. Krawczyk from a car with an HDR video camera, 640x480 @ 30 fps, DR 1e5:1 and 1e7:1; the MPI HDR video cameras (Silicon Vision Lars III, IMS Chips HDRC VGAx) were photometrically calibrated (Krawczyk, Goesele, Seidel). Mantiuk et al. 2004 (research-cache/datasets/papers/mantiuk04pmhdrve.pdf) confirms a Lars III 'returned linear radiance values' and was calibrated 'using a Kodak GrayCard with 80% reflectance' for their sequences.
datasets.night_relevance: Tunnel is a dark->bright driving transition (temporal adaptation), not a night scene

clipping.note: the HDR merge has a hard ceiling (raw 128.875 -> ~36 cd/m^2): every lamp core is CLIPPED, so lamp luminances/energies are LOWER BOUNDS; the scene is NOT a valid photometric reference for the point sources themselves, only for the surround.
